name: Maiden Clean
reference: The clean intros of Revelations (Piece of Mind, 1983, Compass Point Nassau) and Infinite Dreams (Seventh Son of a Seventh Son, 1988, Musicland Munich), both prod. Martin Birch, in the clean Strat sound the owner asked for
rig: No source documents these two clean parts track by track, and no effect settings are published. Nearest evidence: Dave Murray's '57 Stratocaster (documented, Boost Guitar Pedals citing Guitar World); Adrian Smith's HSH Jackson coil-split for a 'Knopfler-y Strat sound' (documented January 1986, use here inferred); Smith's Boss chorus (documented, Guitar World 1983); a Gallien-Krueger 250ML with stereo chorus on Seventh Son (a weak community listing). ToneMirror lists a Dave Murray Stratocaster and a JCM800 2203 for both songs, says to reach the Revelations intro by rolling the guitar volume well back, and names the neck pickup for Infinite Dreams; it gives no clean settings and doesn't say where its numbers come from. Built as a clean Strat into clean Fender amps rather than the Marshalls those sources name, because the owner likes Strat cleans and the rolled-back Marshall distorted far more under the JP70 (experiments D31)
notes: REBUILT (experiments D31) because the 1982 JMP preset wasn't clean under the JP70: THD -11 dB at -12 dBFS input, breakup on every note. Diamond optical compressor first (studio cleans are levelled, and it holds Strat-style picking away from the limiter) -> JP70 pre-voiced as a Strat (`single-coil`) and padded 12 dB, because a Strat pickup puts out less than hot ceramics (the pad size is an estimate; no Strat DI exists here) -> left 1971 Twin Reverb Big Clean on the normal channel, right the same amp on the bright channel -> Twin cabinet IRs with JBL D120s (Clean left, Balanced right). THD at -12 dBFS input: -40 dB at 110 Hz, -33 dB at 330 Hz. The DAW's Clean Chorus (always on for this preset, CC 96-99) at 0.6 Hz, 4 ms, 50 % is the 80s stereo shimmer; those settings are an estimate. One soft 380 ms repeat plus an EMT 140-style plate, at the house reverb level.

chorus.note: Estimate: no settings are documented. The default slow, half-wet 80s chorus.
